newsitem.title: USA: Western U.S. next-day power rises, December lower. [CORRECTED 22:05 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Western U.S. next-day power rises, December lower. [CORRECTED 22:05 GMT]

text.p: Spot bulk electricity prices in the western U.S. rose Monday following outage of a unit at the Diablo Canyon nuclear generating station and higher daily offers from Bonneville Power Administration (BPA).
The 1,087 megawatt (MW) Diablo Canyon nuclear 1 unit in central California was tripped off line late Friday after a fire in an auxiliary power grounding transformer.
A 700 MW unit at the Colstrip coal-fired generating complex near Billings, Montana, resumed operation over the weekend after being shut for a week for unplanned repairs.

BPA, the federal power marketing agency, increased peak load power for Tuesday and Wednesday at the California-Oregon Border (COB) and California-Nevada Border by $2.00 a megawatt hour (MWh) to $32.00 and $32.75, respectively.
"The BPA increase changed the pricing structure in the West," a Southwest trader said.
Forward values of power in the West were lower in line with the NYMEX electricity complex due to outlook of mild weather and softer natural gas prices.
"Gas is off. There's a warming trend. Prices were so high," a New York-based broker said.
December natural gas delivered to the San Juan/Blanco Hub was quoted at $3.45 per million British thermal units, flat from Friday's level.
Firm, peak COB electricity for Tuesday was quoted at $30.00-$32.00, sharply higher than Friday's $27.00-$28.00 for Monday delivery.
Firm, off-peak COB power for Tuesday were notationally pegged at $16.50-$17.50, compared with $15.50-$16.50 Friday.
December COB deliveries were assessed at $27.50-$28.50, and January COB $23.50-$24.25.
First-quarter 1997 COB was valued at $20.00-$20.25, down from Friday's $21.50-$22.00. Second-quarter 1997 COB was talked at $13.50-$14.30. (Corrects from $19.60-$20.00)
Next-day firm, peak power at Mid-Columbia (Mid-C) was discussed at $29.00-$31.00, up from $26.00-$27.50 Friday.
Next-day firm, off-peak Mid-C values were assessed at $18.00-$19.00, higher than Friday's $17.00-$18.00.
December Mid-C was quoted at $25.50-$26.00, while January 1997 Mid-C was pegged at $23.45-$24.00.
Tuesday firm, peak power at the Palo Verde (PV) switchyard in Arizona was talked at $28.50-$30.00, markedly higher than $24.50-$25.50 Friday.
Tuesday firm, off-peak PV electricity was quoted at $15.00-$17.00, up from Friday's $13.00-$14.50.
December PV power was assessed at $26.75-$28.00, and January PV $22.90-$23.50
Four Corners firm, peak deliveries jumped to $29.00-$31.00, up from $25.00-$27.00 Friday.
Four Corners firm, off-peak power climbed to $16.00-$18.00, higher than Friday's $14.00-$16.00.
--R Leong, New York Power Desk +1 212 859 1622
